mainTopic: Using trees and their roots on שבת, and whether someone up a tree may climb down
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: carrying under a tree with low branches is limited to בית סאתים, because the space is a דירה שתשמישה לאויר. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's rule that roots three טפחים above the ground may not be sat on. רבה and רב ששת argue about a root that rises above three טפחים and then comes back down near the ground. רבה permits it because anything that low counts as ground, and רב ששת forbids it because it grows from a forbidden source. The גמרא narrows the dispute to roots running sideways and extends it to trees in a ditch, in a corner, and to אביי's palm tree growing through his roof. An attempted proof from the משנה against רבה is rejected, and a ברייתא teaches that on שבת one may not climb, hang from, or lean on a tree or an animal. Two ברייתות disagree about whether someone up a tree may climb down, and the גמרא gives three ways to settle this. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע then links that disagreement to the argument of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע about mixed blood of קרבנות, which turns on whether acting (קום עשה) or not acting (שב ואל תעשה) is better. The גמרא begins to reject that link, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why carrying under the tree is limited to בית סאתים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its explanation of an earlier ruling. A tree whose branches hang down forms a 'dwelling' used only for open-air purposes, and such a place gets the limit of בית סאתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is a dwelling whose use is for the open air, and in any dwelling whose use is for the open air, one may not carry in it more than an area of בית סאתים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for a ruling it stated on the previous amud. You may carry under a tree with low-hanging branches only within an area of בית סאתים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hanging branches act like walls, but nobody actually lives in that space. It is used only for outdoor things, such as a guard watching a field. Because it is not a real home, חז״ל treated it like a קרפף, which gets the בית סאתים limit.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'dwelling' used only for open-air purposes, not a real place to live
An area of two סאה of seed, about 5,000 square אמות; the limit for carrying in an enclosure that is not a home

steps.whatToRemember: A space surrounded by partitions but not used as a real home, a דירה שתשמישה לאויר, is limited to בית סאתים for carrying.

phrases.english: because it is a dwelling whose use is for the open air,
phrases.notes: It is used only for outdoor purposes, such as guarding fields.

phrases.english: and any dwelling whose use is for the open air —

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְטַלְטְלִין בָּהּ יָתֵר מִבֵּית סָאתַיִם.
phrases.english: one may not carry in it more than an area of two beit se'a.
phrases.notes: It is treated like a קרפף, an enclosure that is not a home.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵי דִּירָה שֶׁתַּשְׁמִישָׁהּ לַאֲוִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reasoning of a ruling stated on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tree-enclosed space is a דירה שתשמישה לאויר, so carrying there is limited to בית סאתים.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about raised roots
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: if a tree's roots are three טפחים above the ground, one may not sit on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if its roots are high above the ground, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. This sets up the discussion about tree roots that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, using a tree is forbidden because of a גזירה that one might come to pluck from it. A root three טפחים or more above the ground counts as part of the tree. A root lower than that is treated like the ground itself.

keyTerms.meaning: High above the ground (here, three טפחים or more)
Etc.; the rest of the quoted text

phrases.english: "Its roots are high above the ground," etc.
phrases.notes: The full משנה line: if they are three טפחים high, one may not sit on them.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׇׁרָשָׁיו גְּבוֹהִין מִן הָאָרֶץ וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Roots three טפחים above the ground may not be sat on during שבת.

steps.title: Dispute over roots that come down from above three handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב ששת argue about roots that rise above three טפחים and then curve back down to within three טפחים of the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: roots of a tree that come from above three טפחים down to within three טפחים of the ground. רבה said it is permitted to use them. רב ששת said it is forbidden to use them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a מחלוקת between אמוראים about a case in between the two rules of the משנה. The root's low part is near the ground, but it comes from a part of the root that is high up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave two clear cases: high roots are forbidden and low roots are permitted. Here a single root has both: it starts high and then dips low. The question is whether we judge the low part by where it is now or by where it came from.

keyTerms.meaning: From above three טפחים to within three טפחים

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that the high part of the root, above three טפחים, is forbidden. The argument is only about the low section that has come back down near the ground.

phrases.english: It was stated: roots of a tree that come
phrases.notes: Opens a dispute between אמוראים.

phrases.english: from above three handbreadths to within three handbreadths,
phrases.notes: The root rises high, then bends back down close to the ground.

phrases.english: Rabba said: it is permitted to use them,

phrases.aramaic: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: אָסוּר לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶן.
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: it is forbidden to use them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: שׇׁרְשֵׁי אִילָן הַבָּאִין מִלְּמַעְלָה מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה לְתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the משנה's three-טפחים rule to an in-between case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה permits using the low part of a root that comes down from above three טפחים; רב ששת forbids it.

steps.title: רבה's reason: anything below three handbreadths is ground
steps.stepSummary: רבה permits the low part because anything less than three טפחים from the ground is legally considered ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said it is permitted to use them, because anything less than three טפחים from the ground is treated as ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבה's ruling, this time adding his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה judges the root only by where it is right now. Below three טפחים, the rule of לבוד says it merges with the ground, so it is no longer considered 'tree' at all. Where the root came from does not matter.

phrases.english: Rabba said: it is permitted to use them,
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats his ruling in order to add the reason.

phrases.english: because anything less than three handbreadths from the ground —
is ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה אָמַר: מוּתָּר לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶן, דְּכׇל פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה דְּאַרְעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבה's position in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anything within three טפחים of the ground is legally ground, regardless of where it came from.

steps.title: רב ששת's reason: it comes from a forbidden source
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת forbids the low part because it grows out of a forbidden part of the tree, so it keeps that forbidden status.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said it is forbidden to use them, because since they come from a forbidden source, they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רב ששת's ruling and adds his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת judges the root by its source. The low section grows out of the high, forbidden section, so it carries that איסור with it. Being close to the ground does not turn it into 'ground.'

keyTerms.meaning: It comes from the force of a forbidden thing

steps.whyThisMatters: The two reasons show a basic split. רבה goes by present location, and רב ששת goes by origin. This sets up the next step, which shows where each logic actually applies.

phrases.aramaic: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: אָסוּר לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶן,
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: it is forbidden to use them,
phrases.notes: The גמרא repeats his ruling in order to add the reason.

phrases.english: because since they come from a forbidden source —
phrases.notes: The source is the part of the root above three טפחים.

phrases.english: they are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר: אָסוּר לְהִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶן, דְּכֵיוָן דְּמִכֹּחַ אִיסּוּר קָאָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for the opposing view, parallel to step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Something that grows out of a forbidden source keeps that forbidden status even when it is near the ground.

steps.title: Narrowing the dispute: upward, downward, and sideways roots
steps.stepSummary: For roots shaped like a rocky crag, those that climb upward are forbidden by all and those that slope downward are permitted by all. Only roots running sideways are the subject of the dispute between רבה and רב ששת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Roots that look like a rocky crag: those that rise upward are forbidden, and those that go down below are permitted. Those that go to the sides are the subject of the dispute between רבה and רב ששת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the dispute to a narrower case. It shows which roots everyone agrees on and which roots the אמוראים actually argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a root's shape climbs upward, it is clearly part of the high, forbidden tree, so everyone forbids it. When it slopes downward toward the ground, everyone treats it as ground and permits it. Only roots spreading sideways are truly in-between, so that is where location (רבה) and origin (רב ששת) give different answers.

keyTerms.meaning: A rocky crag or cliff ledge

steps.whatToRemember: Roots that climb upward are forbidden by all, and roots that slope downward are permitted by all. The מחלוקת of רבה and רב ששת covers only roots spreading sideways.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the מחלוקת covers every root that dips within three טפחים. The גמרא limits it to sideways roots only.

phrases.english: Those that resemble a rocky crag,
phrases.notes: The roots stick up and dip like a jagged ledge.

phrases.english: those that rise upward are forbidden.
phrases.notes: Everyone agrees.

phrases.english: Those that go down below are permitted.
phrases.notes: Everyone agrees.

phrases.english: To the sides is the dispute of Rabba and Rav Sheshet.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּדָמוּ כִּמְשׁוּנִּיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the scope of the dispute presented in steps 3 through 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute between רבה and רב ששת is limited to sideways-spreading roots; upward roots are forbidden by all and downward roots are permitted by all.

steps.title: The same dispute applies to a ditch and a corner
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב ששת also disagree about a tree growing in a ditch and a tree growing in a corner between two walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise a ditch, and likewise in a corner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds two more cases where רבה and רב ששת have the same argument: a tree in a ditch and a tree in a corner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases, part of the tree is closed in by walls, either the banks of the ditch or the two walls of the corner. רבה treats the closed-in part as if it were ground, so the three טפחים just above it can be used. רב ששת does not, because it is all one tree, and the closed-in part does not lose its status as tree.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise, meaning the same dispute applies here
A corner where two walls meet

phrases.english: And likewise, a tree in a ditch,
phrases.notes: The ditch's banks enclose the lower part of the tree.

phrases.english: and likewise, a tree in a corner.
phrases.notes: Two walls enclose the lower part of the tree.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אַנִּיגְרָא, וְכֵן בְּקֶרֶן זָוִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the scope of the dispute between רבה and רב ששת to two new physical situations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The disagreement between רבה and רב ששת also applies to a tree in a ditch and a tree in a corner.

steps.title: אביי's palm tree growing through his roof
steps.stepSummary: אביי had a palm tree that grew up through an opening in his roof. רב יוסף permitted him to use it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain palm tree that belonged to אביי, and it went up through an opening in the roof. He came before רב יוסף, and he permitted it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story. אביי's palm tree grew up through a hole in his roof, and רב יוסף allowed him to use the first three טפחים of the tree above the roof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The part of the tree inside the house is closed in by walls, much like the ditch and corner cases. רב יוסף treated that enclosed part as if it were ground, so the section just above the roof counts as being near the ground and may be used.

keyTerms.meaning: An opening, here a hole in the roof

phrases.english: There was a certain palm tree that belonged to Abaye,
and it went up through an opening in the roof.
He came before Rav Yosef
phrases.notes: אביי came to ask whether he could use the tree on שבת.

phrases.english: and he permitted it to him.
phrases.notes: Meaning the first three טפחים above the roof.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דִּיקְלָא דַּהֲוָה לְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a practical ruling in a case similar to the enclosed-tree cases just mentioned.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף permitted using the part of the palm tree just above the roof.

steps.title: The permission follows רבה
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר תחליפא tells אביי that רב יוסף's permission follows the view of רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר תחליפא said: The one who permitted it to you permitted it to you according to רבה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר תחליפא explains which side of the argument רב יוסף's ruling is based on: רבה, not רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה holds that an enclosed part of a tree counts as ground, so the three טפחים above it are permitted. According to רב ששת, the whole tree keeps its status as tree, and this permission would not work.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of רבה

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Taḥlifa said:
The one who permitted it to you, permitted it to you according to Rabba.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר תַּחְלִיפָא: דִּשְׁרָא לָךְ, כְּרַבָּה שְׁרָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties רב יוסף's practical ruling to one side of the dispute between רבה and רב ששת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף's permission works only according to רבה.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב אחא בר תחליפא needed to say this at all, since it seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אחא בר תחליפא's comment, asking what new point he is teaching. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling clearly treats an enclosed part of a tree as ground, which is exactly רבה's view. So it seems pointless to announce that it follows רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, a challenge that a statement teaches nothing new

phrases.english: Isn't it obvious?

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether step 9 teaches anything new.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר תחליפא's statement that the permission follows רבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case plainly matches רבה's view, so stating it adds no new information.

steps.title: We might have thought a house counts as full of earth
steps.stepSummary: The statement was needed. We might have thought that even רב ששת agrees here, because a house is treated as if it were full, but רב אחא בר תחליפא teaches that it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that even according to רב ששת, a house is considered as if it were full, and one may use the part less than three טפחים from the roof. So he teaches us that this is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new point. Without רב אחא בר תחליפא's comment, we might have thought that רב ששת would also permit this case, because a house is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could argue that a house is viewed as if it were packed with earth up to the roof, which would make the roof like the ground level. Then the first three טפחים above the roof would be permitted even for רב ששת. By saying the ruling follows רבה, רב אחא בר תחליפא teaches that רב ששת rejects this idea and forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said, introducing a mistaken assumption
It is considered as if it were full
He teaches us, introducing the real new point

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's permission for אביי's palm tree works only according to רבה. רב ששת does not treat a house as if it were filled with earth, so for him the part above the roof stays forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: The idea of a house being considered full is the rejected assumption, not the conclusion. רב ששת does not accept it.

phrases.english: You might have said that even according to Rav Sheshet
the house is considered as if it were full,
phrases.notes: As if it were filled with earth up to the roof.

phrases.english: and one may use the part less than three handbreadths near the roof,
so he teaches us that this is not so.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא אֲפִילּוּ לְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge by showing what mistaken assumption the statement rules out.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן: shows the statement rules out a plausible mistake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Even רב ששת would permit it, because a house is treated as if it were filled with earth up to the roof.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב ששת does not treat a house as full, so the permission follows רבה alone.

steps.title: Attempted proof from the משנה that bent-back roots are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, which forbids sitting on roots three טפחים high. It argues that the משנה must mean even roots that bend back down, which would support רב ששת against רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: if the roots are three טפחים above the ground, one may not sit on them. What case is this? If the roots do not bend back down, this is obvious. So doesn't it have to mean that they are forbidden even though they bend back down?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings our משנה as a challenge to רבה. It argues that the משנה only makes sense if it forbids even the low, bent-back part of the roots.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Roots that stay high above three טפחים are clearly part of the tree, so the משנה would not need to say they are forbidden. Since the משנה said it anyway, it seems to teach something new: even the part that curves back down near the ground is forbidden. That is רב ששת's view, and it goes against רבה, whose view רב יוסף followed for אביי's palm tree.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
They bend back down (the roots curve back toward the ground)
Rather, doesn't it mean...? (pushing toward a conclusion)

steps.confusionAlert: The 'it's obvious' argument is not an attack on the משנה. The גמרא uses it as a lever to force the משנה into teaching the stricter case, which would support רב ששת.

phrases.english: We learned: if its roots are higher than the ground
phrases.notes: Quoting our משנה

phrases.english: by three handbreadths, one may not sit on them.
What is the case?
If the roots do not bend back down, that is obvious.
phrases.notes: Roots that stay high are plainly part of the tree

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו, אַף עַל גַּב דְּהָדְרִי כָּיְפִי!
phrases.english: Rather, doesn't it mean even though they bend back down!
phrases.notes: This would support רב ששת

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: שׇׁרָשָׁיו גְּבוֹהִין מִן הָאָרֶץ שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רב יוסף's ruling has been tied to רבה, the גמרא tests רבה's view against the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's view that roots bending back to within three טפחים of the ground may be used.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה would be stating the obvious unless it forbids even bent-back roots, so it must forbid them. That contradicts רבה.

steps.title: The משנה teaches about one side being level with the ground
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The משנה is talking about roots that do not bend back down. Its new point is that sitting on them is forbidden even if on one side of the tree the roots are level with the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really, it is talking about roots that do not bend back down. What it teaches us is that they are forbidden even though on one side the tree is level with the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the proof. The משנה is not obvious after all, because it is teaching a different new point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the claim that the simple case was too obvious to teach. The answer gives the משנה a new point even in the simple case. Even if one side of the tree has roots flush with the ground, which might make you think the whole root area counts as ground, the high roots on the other sides are still forbidden. So the משנה gives no support to רב ששת, and רבה's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us

phrases.english: No, really it is where they do not bend back down,
and this is what it teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּצִידּוֹ אֶחָד שָׁוֶה לָאָרֶץ.
phrases.english: even though one side of it is level with the ground.
phrases.notes: The high roots on the other sides are still forbidden

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעוֹלָם דְּלָא הָדָרִי כָּיְפִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12 by giving the משנה a different new point.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole attempted proof from the משנה against רבה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the simple case was too obvious to teach. In fact the משנה teaches something new even there: one level side does not permit the rest.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms the 'one side level' reading and gives the reason
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the same thing as the rejection: roots three טפחים high, or with a three-טפחים gap beneath them, are forbidden even if one side is level with the ground. The reason is that one may not climb, hang from, or lean on a tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: roots of a tree that are three טפחים above the ground, or that have an empty space of three טפחים beneath them, may not be sat on, even if one side is level with the ground. This is because one may not climb a tree, hang from a tree, or lean on a tree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that uses the exact phrase 'even though one side is level with the ground.' This backs up the reading just given to the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא confirms that 'one side level with the ground' really is the new point being taught, which supports the rejection in step 13. It adds a second case: roots with a hollow space of three טפחים underneath also count as part of the tree. It also explains the root of the law: using a tree on שבת is forbidden, whether by climbing it, hanging from it, or even leaning on it. This rule is a שבות, a rabbinic safeguard.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical הלכה: on שבת one may not climb, hang from, or lean on a tree, and high or hollow-bottomed roots count as part of the tree.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: roots of a tree
that are three handbreadths above the ground

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁיֵּשׁ חָלָל תַּחְתֵּיהֶן שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים,
phrases.english: or that have a hollow space of three handbreadths beneath them,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁצִּידּוֹ אֶחָד שָׁוֶה לָאָרֶץ —
phrases.english: even though one side of it is level with the ground,
phrases.notes: This fits the way the גמרא pushed back the proof in step 13.

phrases.english: one may not sit on them,
because one may not climb a tree,
and one may not hang from a tree,
and one may not lean on a tree.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן שׇׁרְשֵׁי אִילָן שֶׁגְּבוֹהִין מִן הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 13's reading of the משנה with a ברייתא that says the same thing explicitly.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the משנה teaches 'even though one side is level with the ground.'
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that uses that exact phrase.

steps.title: No sitting in a tree all שבת; the same rule for animals; pits and fences are allowed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. One may not climb a tree before שבת and sit there all of שבת. The same rules apply to animals. But one may climb up and down a pit, ditch, cave, or fence, even a hundred אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not go up a tree while it is still day before שבת and sit there the whole day. This applies both to a tree and to any animal. But a pit, a ditch, a cave, or a fence: one may climb up and climb down, even if they are a hundred אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going and adds more rules about using trees and animals on שבת, then gives a contrasting case where climbing is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even climbing up before שבת does not help. Sitting in the tree on שבת is itself using the tree, so it is forbidden. Animals follow the same rule: no riding, hanging from, or leaning on them. The pit, cave, and fence case shows that the problem is not the effort of climbing. The problem is using a tree or an animal, so climbing other things is allowed even for a great distance.

keyTerms.meaning: While it is still day (before שבת begins)

steps.whatToRemember: On שבת one may not use a tree or an animal by climbing it, hanging from it, leaning on it, or even sitting in it after climbing up before שבת. Climbing a pit, ditch, cave, or fence is fine, even very far. Roots three טפחים high, or with a three-טפחים gap beneath them, count as the tree, even if one side is level with the ground.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the prohibition is about hard physical effort. The pit and fence case proves that even a hundred אמות of climbing is allowed. What is forbidden is using a tree or an animal specifically.

phrases.english: And one may not climb a tree while it is still day
and sit there the entire day.
phrases.notes: Sitting there is itself using the tree

phrases.english: This applies both to a tree and to any animal,
but a pit, a ditch, a cave, or a fence:
one may climb up and climb down,
even if they are a hundred cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא יַעֲלֶה בְּאִילָן מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, adding related rules and a contrasting permitted case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not sit in a tree on שבת even if one climbed up before שבת. Trees and animals share these rules. Climbing a pit, ditch, cave, or fence is permitted even for a hundred אמות.

steps.title: Two teachings contradict each other about climbing down
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says that a person who climbed a tree may climb down. Another ברייתא says he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: if he climbed up, he is allowed to come down. Another ברייתא teaches: he is forbidden to come down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts two ברייתות side by side that seem to contradict each other about a person already up in a tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 taught that one may not use a tree on שבת. So the question is what happens once someone is already up there. Coming down is also a use of the tree, so it is unclear which ruling is right.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in one ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in one ברייתא:
If he climbed up, he is permitted to climb down,
and it was taught in another: he is forbidden to climb down.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא אִם עָלָה מוּתָּר לֵירֵד וְתָנֵי חֲדָא אָסוּר לֵירֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ban on using trees from the ברייתא in steps 14-15, and asks about someone already up a tree.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about climbing down
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same case seems to get opposite rulings.

steps.title: It depends on when he climbed up
steps.stepSummary: If he climbed before שבת began, he may come down. If he climbed after nightfall on שבת, he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, he climbed while it was still day. There, he climbed after it got dark.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying each ברייתא talks about a different time of climbing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Climbing before שבת was allowed, so coming down is allowed too. Climbing on שבת was forbidden, so the person is not allowed to benefit from it by climbing down.

keyTerms.meaning: While it was still day (before שבת)
After it got dark (once שבת began)

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, he climbed while it was still day;
there, he climbed after nightfall.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא כָּאן מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם כָּאן מִשֶּׁחָשֵׁיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction from step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to discuss the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Climbing before שבת means he may come down. Climbing on שבת means he may not.

steps.title: It depends on whether he climbed by mistake or on purpose
steps.stepSummary: Both ברייתות talk about climbing on שבת. A person who climbed by mistake may come down, and a person who climbed on purpose may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say: both talk about after dark, and it is still not difficult. Here, he climbed by mistake. There, he climbed on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the same contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both cases take place on שבת. The difference is the person's intent. The deliberate climber is penalized and must stay up, while the mistaken climber is not.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces an alternative answer)
Both this one and that one

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
both this and that are after nightfall,
and it is not difficult:
here, he climbed by mistake;
there, he climbed on purpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא הָא וְהָא מִשֶּׁחָשֵׁיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second resolution in place of step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Climbing on שבת always means he may not come down.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only someone who climbed on purpose may not come down. Someone who climbed by mistake may.

steps.title: Both talk about a mistake, and they argue about penalizing
steps.stepSummary: Both ברייתות talk about someone who climbed by mistake. They disagree about whether חכמים penalize a mistaken person to protect against deliberate ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you want, say: both talk about a mistake. Here they argue whether we penalize the mistaken person because of the deliberate one. One master holds that we penalize, and the other master holds that we do not penalize.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer. Instead of splitting the cases, it says the two ברייתות are a real argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is now identical in both: a mistaken climb on שבת. The view that forbids coming down holds that חכמים penalize even the mistaken person, so that deliberate climbers cannot claim it was a mistake. The view that permits coming down holds there is no such penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: Penalizing a mistaken person because of a deliberate one

steps.confusionAlert: Here the ברייתות are no longer talking about different cases. They are two opposing opinions about the very same case.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of קנסו שוגג אטו מזיד comes up all over ש״ס. This step turns it into the real point of the argument.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
both this and that are by mistake,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא בְּקָנְסוּ שׁוֹגֵג אַטּוּ מֵזִיד קָמִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: and here they disagree whether they penalized the mistaken person because of the deliberate one.
One master holds: we penalize.
And the other master holds: we do not penalize.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא הָא וְהָא בְּשׁוֹגֵג וְהָכָא בְּקָנְסוּ שׁוֹגֵג אַטּוּ מֵזִיד קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third resolution. It turns the contradiction into a real argument about penalties.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making it a dispute (the ברייתות truly argue)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות must be talking about different cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: Same case. They argue whether חכמים penalize a mistaken person because of deliberate ones.

steps.title: This argument matches an argument of תנאים about mixed blood
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says the two ברייתות about whether one may climb down from the tree match an argument between תנאים. He begins quoting a source about blood of קרבנות that got mixed together.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, son of רב יהושע, said: it is like an argument of תנאים. Blood that is put on the מזבח once, which got mixed with other blood that is put on once, should be put on once. Blood that is put on four times, mixed with other blood that is put on four times, should be put on four times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a parallel. This line starts the quote, and the next lines will reach the cases where the תנאים actually argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the source only gives the easy cases, where both kinds of blood need the same treatment. The real argument comes when one-time blood gets mixed with four-time blood. The point that ties it to the tree case is not a penalty for a mistake. It is the question of whether acting (קום עשה) or not acting (שב ואל תעשה) is better, which step 27 spells out.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like an argument between תנאים
A single application of blood on the מזבח
Four applications of blood (on all sides of the מזבח)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
It is like a dispute of the Tanna'im.
Blood that is applied with one application
that got mixed with blood applied with one application,
should be applied with one application;
four applications mixed with four applications,
should be applied with four applications.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ כְּתַנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the contradiction between the two ברייתות about climbing down (step 16) to an argument between תנאים about blood of קרבנות. Step 27 explains that the link is acting vs. not acting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two ברייתות about whether one may climb down from a tree match an argument between תנאים. The quoted source opens with simple cases of mixed blood.

steps.title: The case of mixed blood and the two opinions
steps.stepSummary: Blood needing four sprinklings got mixed with blood needing one sprinkling. רבי אליעזר says to sprinkle four times; רבי יהושע says to sprinkle once.
steps.simpleTranslation: If blood that needs four sprinklings got mixed with blood that needs one sprinkling: רבי אליעזר says it should be sprinkled four times, and רבי יהושע says it should be sprinkled once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting the source that רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע started in step 20. Here we reach the actual argument between the תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some קרבנות, like an עולה, need their blood sprinkled four times on the מזבח. Others, like a בכור, need only one sprinkling. Once the two bloods are mixed, the mixture cannot satisfy both rules perfectly, so רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע disagree about which rule to follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood that must be sprinkled four times (on the corners of the מזבח)
Blood that needs only one sprinkling
A sprinkling or placing of blood

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is still part of the source that רב הונא is quoting to explain the tree-climbing argument from steps 16-20.

phrases.english: Blood needing four sprinklings mixed with blood needing one sprinkling,
phrases.notes: For example, the blood of an עולה mixed with the blood of a בכור

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: יִנָּתְנוּ בְּמַתַּן אַרְבַּע.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: it should be sprinkled four times.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: יִנָּתְנוּ בְּמַתָּנָה אַחַת.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua says: it should be sprinkled once.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתַּן אַרְבַּע בְּמַתַּן אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the source quotation begun in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: sprinkle four times. רבי יהושע: sprinkle once.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: sprinkling once breaks בל תגרע
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר attacks רבי יהושע: if you sprinkle only once, you leave out sprinklings that the four-sprinkling קרבן needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: But he is breaking the rule of 'do not take away'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר challenges רבי יהושע's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah forbids leaving out parts of a מצוה (בל תגרע). The four-sprinkling קרבן is supposed to get four sprinklings, so giving the mixture only one sprinkling seems to take away from its מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition against taking away from a מצוה

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:
But he is breaking 'do not take away'!
phrases.notes: Because the four-sprinkling קרבן loses three of its sprinklings

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הֲרֵי הוּא עוֹבֵר עַל בַּל תִּגְרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יהושע's ruling from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's ruling to sprinkle only once
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sprinkling only once leaves out sprinklings that the four-sprinkling קרבן requires, which breaks בל תגרע.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: sprinkling four times breaks בל תוסיף
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers with a counter-attack: if you sprinkle four times, you add extra sprinklings to the one-sprinkling קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: But he is breaking the rule of 'do not add'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע turns the same kind of argument back on רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah also forbids adding extra parts to a מצוה (בל תוסיף). The one-sprinkling קרבן should get only one sprinkling, so sprinkling four times adds three extra. Both opinions now seem to break a prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition against adding to a מצוה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
But he is breaking 'do not add'.
phrases.notes: Because the one-sprinkling קרבן gets three extra sprinklings

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הֲרֵי הוּא עוֹבֵר בְּבַל תּוֹסִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A counter-challenge that answers step 22 by showing that רבי אליעזר's view has the same kind of problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling to sprinkle four times
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sprinkling four times adds sprinklings to the one-sprinkling קרבן, which breaks בל תוסיף.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: בל תוסיף applies only to unmixed blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר defends himself: the prohibition against adding applies only when the blood stands by itself, not when it is mixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: They only said this rule (do not add) when the blood is by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers רבי יהושע's attack from step 23.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He limits בל תוסיף. When you add sprinklings to blood that is by itself, you break the rule. In a mixture, though, the extra sprinklings are given for the sake of the other blood, so nothing is really being 'added.'

keyTerms.meaning: They only said (the rule applies only in this case)
When it is by itself (not mixed)

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said:
They only said it (do not add) when it is by itself.
phrases.notes: Meaning the blood is not part of a mixture

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לֹא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁהוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the בל תוסיף challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sprinkling four times on a mixture breaks בל תוסיף.
steps.terutzMaskana: בל תוסיף applies only to blood that is by itself, so a mixture is not included.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: then בל תגרע also applies only to unmixed blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע uses the same logic: the prohibition against taking away also applies only when the blood is by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: 'Do not take away' was also said only when the blood is by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע takes רבי אליעזר's own answer and uses it to defend his own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a mixture is outside בל תוסיף, then by the same reasoning it is also outside בל תגרע. That removes רבי אליעזר's attack from step 22, and the two sides are now even.

keyTerms.meaning: It was not said (the rule was not stated except for...)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
'Do not take away' was not said
except when it is by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לֹא נֶאֱמַר בַּל תִּגְרַע אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁהוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי אליעזר's limitation from step 24 to answer the בל תגרע challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sprinkling once on a mixture breaks בל תגרע.
steps.terutzMaskana: Just like בל תוסיף, בל תגרע applies only to blood that is by itself, so sprinkling a mixture once breaks nothing.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: better to break a rule by doing nothing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע adds an argument: sprinkling four times breaks בל תוסיף through an action, while sprinkling once breaks בל תגרע only by not acting. Not acting is better.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע also said: When you sprinkle, you break 'do not add' and you did an act with your hand. When you do not sprinkle, you break 'do not take away' but you did not do an act with your hand.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע gives a second reason for his view, one that works even if both prohibitions would apply. This sets up how the גמרא will connect the argument to the tree-climbing case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if we say both rules apply to the mixture, the two violations are not equal. Adding sprinklings is an active deed, while leaving them out is just staying passive (שב ואל תעשה). When every choice breaks some rule, the passive choice is better.

keyTerms.meaning: An action with your own hand (an active deed)
Sit and do nothing (breaking a rule passively); this is a concept, not a phrase from the text

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר says four sprinklings and רבי יהושע says one. Each side's charge (בל תגרע vs. בל תוסיף) is answered by the idea that these rules apply only to blood by itself. רבי יהושע adds that breaking a rule passively is better than breaking it with an action.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of choosing passivity (שב ואל תעשה) over active violation is the tool רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע will use to tie this argument to the question of whether someone who climbed a tree on שבת may climb down.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua said further:
When you sprinkled (four times), you broke 'do not add'
and you did an act with your hand.
When you did not sprinkle (four times), you broke 'do not take away'
but you did not do an act with your hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent argument for רבי יהושע's view after the two sides were left even in steps 24-25.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע's ruling to sprinkle the mixture only once
steps.raayaSupportSource: The logic that a passive violation (שב ואל תעשה) is better than an active violation

steps.title: Linking the tree case to the blood-sprinkling debate
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion: according to רבי אליעזר, who prefers קום עשה, the person climbs down from the tree. According to רבי יהושע, who prefers שב ואל תעשה, he stays up.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אליעזר, who said there that 'get up and act' is better, here too he should climb down. According to רבי יהושע, who said there that 'sit and do nothing' is better, here too he should not climb down.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע completes his parallel by applying the debate about mixed blood to a person who is up in a tree on שבת. Climbing down is an action that breaks a rule, while staying up breaks a rule only by not acting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the blood case, רבי אליעזר chose the option that involves doing something, and רבי יהושע chose the option that involves doing nothing. The tree case has the same choice: climb down (an action) or stay put (no action). So the suggestion is that each תנא's ruling carries over directly.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Get up and act': breaking a rule by doing something
'Sit and do nothing': breaking a rule only by not acting
There (in the other case, the blood sprinklings)

steps.confusionAlert: Each side of the blood debate now gets matched to one side of the tree case. רבי אליעזר goes with 'climb down' because climbing down is the action. רבי יהושע goes with 'stay up' because staying up is not acting.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Eliezer, who said there
'get up and act' is better,
here too he should climb down.
According to Rabbi Yehoshua, who said there
'sit and do nothing' is better,
here too he should not climb down.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דְּאָמַר הָתָם ״קוּם עֲשֵׂה״ עָדִיף, הָכִי נָמֵי יֵרֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב הונא's comparison from step 20. It applies the principle from step 26 (whether acting or not acting is better) to the two ברייתות about climbing down in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling for someone up a tree on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The מחלוקת of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע about mixed blood (קום עשה vs. שב ואל תעשה)

steps.title: רבי אליעזר may prefer action only when a מצוה is done
steps.stepSummary: The comparison is rejected. רבי אליעזר may prefer acting only because, in the blood case, the action also does a מצוה. Climbing down a tree does no מצוה, so even he would say not to climb down.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps that is not so. רבי אליעזר only said there that 'get up and act' is better because he is doing a מצוה. But here, where he is not doing a מצוה, he would agree that the person should not climb down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison from the previous step. It shows that רבי אליעזר's view may not carry over to the tree case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the blood case, the extra sprinklings are still part of performing a מצוה, so acting has a positive side. In the tree case, climbing down gains no מצוה at all. Without that positive side, רבי אליעזר may also prefer doing nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps that is not so (the comparison may be wrong)
He only said this as far as (a limited case)
A commandment or good deed being done

phrases.english: Perhaps that is not so,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָתָם
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer only said there
that 'get up and act' is better
because he is doing a מצוה.
But here, where he is not doing a מצוה,
he would agree he should not climb down.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּילְמָא לָא הִיא, עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the רבי אליעזר half of the comparison made in Step 27.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי אליעזר would say the person climbs down from the tree
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The cases are different: in the blood case the action does a מצוה, but climbing down from a tree does not.

steps.title: Second rejection: רבי יהושע's view may also be limited
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a second, separate way to reject the comparison. It will show that רבי יהושע's preference for not acting may also be limited to the blood case. This passage ends before the reason is given.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or alternatively: רבי יהושע only said there that 'sit and do nothing' is better because...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second way to break the comparison, this time focusing on רבי יהושע. It is setting up the next move, and the reason continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first rejection attacked the רבי אליעזר side. This one uses the same pattern to argue that רבי יהושע's view may apply only to the special situation of the blood case. If it does, he might allow climbing down from the tree.

phrases.english: Or alternatively,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָתָם
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua only said there
that 'sit and do nothing' is better
only because...

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי נָמֵי, עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, alternative rejection of Step 27, this time limiting רבי יהושע's view instead of רבי אליעזר's.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי יהושע would say the person stays up in the tree
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יהושע's preference for not acting may depend on details of the blood case. The reason continues on the next amud.
